newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners wade through flood of foreign crudes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners wade through flood of foreign crudes.

text.p: U.S. refiners continued to wade through a flood of foreign crudes Tuesday, reflecting the wide open transatlantic arbitrage, traders said.
The spread between benchmarks West Texas Intermediate and North Sea Brent stood around a $1.70-80 a barrel, maintaining the flow of cargoes from the North Sea and West Africa to the Gulf Coast.
Brent for February 20-25 delivery was heard on offer at March WTI minus 10-30 cents, traders said.

West African Qua Iboe and Forcadoes for early March were on offer at a relatively pricey March plus 60 cents delivered, although traders said the grades' heavy heating oil content brightens their appeal at the moment.
Traders characterized demand as anywhere from "firm" to "soft" amid turnarounds and weak margins.
Yesterday's sharp selloff on the NYMEX seemed to put some refiners on edge. "When the market heads south, refiners walk away," one trader said.

In Latin America, an equity producer sold another cargo of Cusiana at an unconfirmed March WTI minus 50-55 cents a barrel fob. The grade sold Monday at a steep discount of March minus 60 for end-January.
Separately, Colombia's state-owned Ecopetrol is accepting bids tomorrow on a Cusiana cargo for February 12-16.
Meanwhile, a Vasconia cargo for January 19-20 is still looking for a home, with traders saying the cargo is likely to ultimately get done at a discount of around $2.50 to WTI.
In the U.S. aftermarket, a series of partial paper March Brents traded at $22.92/22.93/22.95/22.97 a barrel, weaker compared to the IPE settlement of $22.98.
Feb/March Brent changed hands twice at 35 cents, down three cents from the London close.
